# A test that reads the temporary directory keeps its cached result when the
# variables name another directory. A macOS runner names a different one on
# each machine. Windows reads TMP and TEMP, and the other systems TMPDIR.

mkdir $WORK/tmp1 $WORK/tmp2
env TMPDIR=$WORK/tmp1
env TMP=$WORK/tmp1
env TEMP=$WORK/tmp1
go test ./t
stdout '^ok\s+m/t\s+[0-9.]+s$'
env TMPDIR=$WORK/tmp2
env TMP=$WORK/tmp2
env TEMP=$WORK/tmp2
go test ./t
stdout '^ok\s+m/t\s+\(cached\)'

# Another variable the test reads still decides the result.
env OTHER=changed
go test ./t
! stdout '\(cached\)'

-- go.mod --
module m

go 1.20
-- t/t_test.go --
package t

import (
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"testing"
)

func TestTemp(t *testing.T) {
	file := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "scratch")
	if err := os.WriteFile(file, []byte("x"), 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if _, err := os.ReadFile(file); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	t.Log(os.TempDir(), os.Getenv("OTHER"))
}
